comparison: Perfect agreement on CCEN design and characterization (C16-C19, C23, C25, C56-C57, C64-C69, C71-C72). Both evaluations find the chimeric construct successfully developed and well-documented. OpenEval emphasizes experimental evidence details while peer reviewers confirm successful replacement of Widom 601 DNA with centromeric sequences.

Perfect agreement on microtubule binding assay controls (C27-C29, C60). Both evaluations support the functional assembly data. OpenEval highlights statistical significance (p<10^-6) while peer reviewers treat this as confirmatory validation of the experimental system rather than novel findings.

Strong agreement on OA-mediated force transduction findings (C3, C20, C30-C31, C36, C62). Both find the optical trap data convincing and well-supported. OpenEval notes the ~43% increase in rupture force; peer reviewers emphasize this 'convincingly demonstrates' centromere-histone core contribution to force transduction. Peer R2 includes C58 not in OpenEval R3.

Agreement on Mif2 negative result (C21, C32-C33, C48). Both accept the lack of significant difference as valid. OpenEval calls it 'properly reported'; peer reviewers note it was 'somewhat unexpected' and 'cannot currently be reconciled with structural knowledge' but do not question the data quality. Peer R3 excludes C63 that OpenEval R4 includes.

Strong agreement on DNA sequence contribution to force transduction (C4, C22, C37). Both evaluations support this conclusion. OpenEval emphasizes differential OA behavior and literature context; peer reviewers confirm centromeric DNA increases attachment strength. OpenEval R5 includes C58 not in peer R5.

Agreement on speculative nature of mechanistic proposals (C38-C39). Both mark these as UNCERTAIN/speculative. OpenEval notes additional experiments needed to distinguish mechanisms; peer reviewers state 'how centromeric DNA exerts this effect remains unclear' and requires future investigation. Peer R6 includes additional speculative claims (C50, C52, C63) not in OpenEval R6.

Partial overlap on Mif2 interpretation (C50, C52). OpenEval R7 addresses broader Mif2 discussion (C41-C47, C49-C52) and finds interpretation reasonable given literature; peer R6 groups some Mif2 speculation (C50, C52) with other uncertain mechanistic claims (C38-C39, C63). Different grouping strategies for overlapping speculative content.

Overlap on methodological advance (C59). OpenEval R11 addresses multiple methodological claims (C24, C26, C34-C35, C59, C61, C70, C73) as well-documented; peer R7 specifically highlights C59 as making the assay 'more closely resemble the in vivo situation' and calls it a 'valuable addendum' though with 'limited scope' beyond specialists.

OpenEval R8 evaluates structural biology literature assessment (C53-C55) as well-supported with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found - peer reviewers did not separately evaluate the literature review claims.

OpenEval R9 evaluates background claims about prior W601 work and study motivation (C1-C2, C11-C15) as accurately summarizing published work. No corresponding peer review evaluation found - peer reviewers did not separately assess background/motivation claims.

OpenEval R10 evaluates foundational background knowledge about centromeres and kinetochores (C5-C10) as well-established and appropriately cited. No corresponding peer review evaluation found - peer reviewers did not separately evaluate general background claims.
